corinthians1.12.p1.b1.text: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.

corinthians1.12.p1.b2.text: … when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols …

corinthians1.12.p1.b3.text: … and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.

corinthians1.12.p2.b4.text: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

corinthians1.12.p2.b5.text: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

corinthians1.12.p3.b6.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

corinthians1.12.p3.b7.text: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.

corinthians1.12.p4.b8.text: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. … So it is with Christ.

corinthians1.12.p4.b9.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free …

corinthians1.12.p5.b10.text: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

corinthians1.12.p5.b11.text: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

corinthians1.12.p6.b12.text: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

corinthians1.12.p6.b13.text: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

corinthians1.12.p6.b14.text: … But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it …
